confirmed: The source is arXiv:2505.21396v2 dated 28 February 2026, with 25 PDF pages and Appendices A-K; the title-page footer identifies NeurIPS 2025. Title and authors match the form (PDF p. 1; appendices pp. 11-25).

No randomized human-assistance study is reported. Section 6 describes a within-person comparison without stating randomized topic-to-condition assignment or condition order; the form's S1 design_class other and assignment.randomized not_stated are supported. Random sampling concerns excess output pairing, not assistance allocation (PDF pp. 7-8, sections 6.1-6.2; p. 18, Appendix I.2; p. 25, Figure 4; full markdown including Appendices A-K read).

The paper reports 23 recruited people: 19 undergraduate or graduate students and 4 PhD-holding senior researchers. It does not separately state a randomized or analyzed headcount, so those numerical fields remain null; this recruited cohort cannot meet the 50-person minimum (PDF p. 7, section 6.1; p. 8, section 6.2).

Participants choose two of four topics and propose one idea per topic, receiving three generated reference ideas plus data and validation material for one topic and no reference ideas for the other; Internet/literature search is permitted in the latter condition and LLM use is prohibited (PDF pp. 7-8, section 6.1).

The 20-minute duration per selected topic is explicitly stated (PDF p. 18, Appendix I.2). The submission interface includes research-question, theory, and hypotheses fields and displays references while the participant writes (PDF p. 25, Figure 4).

The references come from GPT-Researcher with metadata and Claude-3.5-Sonnet selection using validation. GPT-4o is gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and Claude is claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022; the footnote says these model versions apply throughout (PDF p. 5, Implementation Details and footnote 2; p. 8, section 6.1).

S1-O1 reported values are exact: Overall, w. Reference 39.1%, Tie 28.3%, w/o Reference 32.6%. The one_line_finding accurately labels these as expert comparisons and 23 as recruits (PDF pp. 7-8, section 6.1 and Table 6a).
S1-O2 reported values are exact: Novelty, w. Reference 43.5%, Tie 23.9%, w/o Reference 32.6% (PDF p. 8, Table 6a).
S1-O3 reported values are exact: Feasibility, w. Reference 50.0%, Tie 17.4%, w/o Reference 32.6% (PDF p. 8, Table 6a).

Table 6a reports pairwise expert preferences, not mean quality scores, and supplies no test statistic, p-value, interval, or explicit total of evaluated pairs/ratings. Ideas are paired within topics and surplus ideas receive sampled comparators; do not infer the human sample or evaluation denominator from the percentages (PDF p. 8, section 6.2 and Table 6a; p. 19, Figure 2).

S2, S4, and S5 are model-generation/selection/validation studies. The 18 annotators in section 4.4 are evaluators, not assisted human ideators; the 50 ideas per method per topic, 10 topics, and top 5 selections are output/task counts (PDF pp. 4-6, sections 4.3-4.4; p. 7, section 5.3; pp. 14-15, Appendix F).
S3 uses 8 published papers and 10 generated ideas per paper topic, not 8 or 10 human participants (PDF p. 7, section 5.2).
This is primary empirical work, not a synthesis; no pooled study count, pooled standardized effect, or pooled interval should be added to synthesis (PDF pp. 4-8, sections 4-6; pp. 14-15, Appendix F).
summary: The arXiv v2 source reports a 23-recruit within-person human study with no stated randomization or separate analyzed count, and the recorded percentages are accurate. Corrections add two omitted output ratings, complete assistance and contrast metadata, and classify the published-idea comparison as AI-versus-human context; core eligibility remains no.
